text: {"status":"CONFLICT","claims":[{"text":"A personal Dropbox is prohibited for company information classified Internal or above.","evidence_id":"E1","quote":"Uploading company information classified Internal or above to a personal cloud-storage account, such as a personal Dropbox, personal Google Drive or personal OneDrive, is prohibited."},{"text":"Internal information may be stored in a personal cloud-storage account for remote work if the account has multi-factor authentication.","evidence_id":"E2","quote":"Employees may store Internal information in a personal cloud-storage account when working remotely, provided the account is protected with multi-factor authentication."},{"text":"Confidential information may only be stored in company-managed systems approved by Information Security and must never be stored in personal cloud-storage accounts.","evidence_id":"E3","quote":"Confidential and Restricted information may only be stored in company-managed systems approved by Information Security. It must never be stored on personal devices or in personal accounts, including personal email and personal cloud-storage accounts."},{"text":"The approved storage locations for company work are the company's managed OneDrive and SharePoint.","evidence_id":"E4","quote":"The company's managed OneDrive and SharePoint are the approved storage locations for company work."}],"conflict_evidence_ids":["E1","E2"],"conflict_note":"E1 says uploading company information classified Internal or above to a personal Dropbox is prohibited, while E2 says Internal information may be stored in personal cloud storage for remote work if multi-factor authentication is enabled."}
